Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Linear Systems and Matrices

Bike Shop Matrices

Organising a whole inventory in one grid

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Matrix Operations
Standards
HSN-VM.C.6, HSN-VM.C.8, HSN-VM.C.10

Students add, subtract, scale and multiply matrices, find 2×2 determinants and inverses, and use a bike shop’s inventory and price matrices to see why matrix multiplication works the way it does.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Add, subtract and multiply matrices by a scalar.
  • Multiply two matrices when the dimensions allow it.
  • Find the determinant of a 2×2 matrix.
  • Find the inverse of a 2×2 matrix and check it.

3Essential question

How can one grid of numbers, multiplied by another, answer a whole set of questions at once?

5MTB connection

A bike shop tracks stock by store and model: a matrix. Multiplying the stock matrix by a price column gives every store’s stock value in one step, which is exactly what inventory software does.

Scalar multiplication models a sale (multiply prices by 0.85 for 15% off); adding matrices combines two deliveries.

The mathOn the trail
MatrixStock by shop and model
Matrix additionAdding a delivery to stock
Scalar multipleA storewide discount
Matrix productStock value of every shop at once

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Run the Bike Shop

Use matrix operations to manage two shops’ stock and value.

You’ll need: The stock and price data (in the foundation); Calculator (matrix mode optional)

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
